messages.subject: read_chunk() not executed
parts:

parts:
Re-submitting with clearer formatting, apologies for the duplication.

I think I've worked out what was causing my problem and it was an extraneous space (' ') in the R code header section.

I've attempted to create a minimal reproducible example using the knitr-manual.Rnw by placing the first code chunk in the file '../child/car-demo.R' and removing the remainder of the document....

../child/car-demo.R

## @knitr cars-demo                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
fit=lm(dist~speed,data=cars) # linear regression                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
par(mar=c(4, 4, 1, .1), mgp=c(2,1,0))
with(cars,plot(speed,dist,panel.last=abline(fit)))
text(10,100,'$Y = \\beta_0 + \\beta_1x + \\epsilon$')
library(ggplot2)
qplot(speed, dist, data=cars)+geom_smooth()

knitr-manual-works.Rnw

\begin{document}
<<setup, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE>>=
library(knitr)
## set global chunk options                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
opts_chunk$set(fig.path='figure/manual-', cache.path='cache/manual-', fig.align='center', fig.show='hold', par=TRUE)
## I use = but I can replace it with <-; set code/output width to be 68                                                                                                                                                                                                      
options(replace.assign=TRUE, width=68)
## tune details of base graphics (http://yihui.name/knitr/hooks)                                                                                                                                                                                                             
knit_hooks$set(par=function(before, options, envir){
if (before && options$fig.show!='none') par(mar=c(4,4,.1,.1),cex.lab=.95,cex.axis=.9,mgp=c(2,.7,0),tcl=-.3)
})
## Read in the cars-demo.R file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
read_chunk("child/cars-demo.R")
@                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\title{knitr: A General-Purpose Tool for Dynamic Report Generation in R}


\author{Yihui Xie}

\maketitle

\section{Hello World}

A natural question is why to reinvent the wheel. The short answer
is that extending Sweave by hacking \textsf{SweaveDrivers.R} in the
\textbf{utils} package is a difficult job to me. Many features in
\textbf{knitr} come naturally as users would have expected. Figure
\ref{fig:cars-demo} is a simple demo of some features of \textbf{knitr}.

\begin{figure}
<<cars-demo,dev='png',fig.width=4,fig.height=2.8,out.width='.45\\textwidth',message=FALSE,cache=TRUE>>=
@                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\caption{\label{fig:cars-demo}A simple demo of possible output in \textbf{knitr}:
(1) multiple plots per chunk; (2) no need to \emph{print()} objects
in \textbf{ggplot2}; (3) device size is $4\times2.8$ (inches) but
output size is adjusted to \texttt{.45\textbackslash{}textwidth} in
chunk options; (4) base graphics and \textbf{ggplot2} can sit side
by side; (5) use the \emph{tikz()} device in \textbf{tikzDevice} by
setting chunk option \texttt{dev='tikz'} (hence can write native \protect\LaTeX{}
expressions in R plots); (6) code highlighting.}
\end{figure}

\end{document}

The _only_ difference between knitr-manual-works.Rnw and knitr-manual-problem.Rnw is the space after '<<cars-demo ,' which prevents the cars-demo.R code from being executed.  Perhaps this is because there is no space in the header line of cars-demo.R at '## @knitr cars-demo' ?

I had a tentative look at read_chunk() to see if I could work out where the '## @knitr cars-demo' might be parsed to see if it had additional white space stripped from it, but couldn't work it out.  Similarly I couldn't work out where in the knit() the labels within '<<cars-demo,dev='png'>>' might be parsed but couldn't work that out either.

Now I know about this I will be attentive to not including unnecessary white space within <<>> sections, but is this behaviour intended?  I tend to usually place spaces after commas (',') to make my code more readable (although in this instance I accidentally placed the space before the comma).  If its intended behaviour then documenting this would be useful (sorry if I've missed this), if not is it possible to parse white space from the labels so that they match?

Regards

Neil
